plot: On a busy school-drop-off morning with a broken traffic light, Bolt blocks the main street and won't say why while Bertha, Turbo and Grumpy blame and honk at him; Pip hears a quack and, being small, looks under Bolt's bumper: he was shielding a mother duck and three ducklings scared by the honking; everyone goes quiet, the ducks reach the pond, Bertha makes the bell just in time; lesson: before you blame, look at what they see; then a note says the school needs a crossing guard and Turbo wants the job.

script.title: Why Is Everyone Mad at Bolt?!

set.place: Wheelburg main street, school drop-off on a Monday morning (broken traffic light)

script.description: Bolt blocks the busy street at school time and everyone is cross with him. Inspector Bolt #13

beats.say: Honk honk! Bolt, move! You are making us late for school!
Why is Bolt blocking every single car on the street?

beats.text: WHY IS EVERYONE MAD AT BOLT?

beats.say: Shh. Please, everyone. Just wait one more minute.
It was Monday morning on Wheelburg's main street. School drop-off time.
The traffic light was broken. And Inspector Bolt stood in the middle.
I have twelve little cars inside me going to school!
The school bell rings in five minutes!
And today the kids sing the morning song together!
Bolt is being bossy again. Procedure, procedure, procedure!
Turbo, please. Not so loud right now.
Loud? I am not loud! HONK! HONK! HONK!
Then, under all the honking, there was one tiny sound.
Wait. Did anyone else hear a little quack?
That was Bertha's squeaky brakes. Everybody knows that.
My brakes do NOT quack, thank you very much!
And look. Bolt keeps looking down at the road. Why?
Pip was right. Bolt's eyes kept going down, down, down.
Hmph. A car stuck in the road is a job for me.
I could tow you to the side. Nice and slow.
No, Grumpy. Please don't move me. Not yet.
Bolt, you always help us. Why won't you help us now?
I am helping, Bertha. I promise. I just can't explain loudly.
Can't explain? Fine. Then I'll just zoom around you!
Turbo, STOP! Stay right where you are!
Turbo stopped so fast that his tires squeaked.
See? Bossy! He shouted at me! In front of everyone!
Only two minutes! My little ones will miss the morning song!
Everyone was cross. Everyone was honking. And Bolt felt very small.
I tried to help. Now everybody thinks I am the problem.
I know that feeling. It's the worst feeling in town.
So tell us, Inspector. What is going on?
If I shout, something very small will get scared.
Something small? The only small thing here is Pip!
Hey! I am small, but I'm not scared of anything!
Bertha's little passengers pressed their noses to her windows.
The kids are asking why the inspector looks so sad.
Tell them I'm not sad. Just... waiting for someone slow.
Waiting for someone slow? Now that is very mysterious.
Slow? Who is slower than a broken traffic light?
Turbo tried to sneak past on the other side.
Turbo, please. Back up. Very gently.
Gently? I don't have a gentle button!
But Turbo backed up. Slowly. For the first time in his life.
That's enough waiting. I'm counting to three. Then I tow.
One...
If we don't go now, the kids miss the song!
Two...
Wait, Grumpy! Small cars are good at one thing. Looking under stuff!
So Pip rolled very low and very slow toward Bolt.
Gently, Pip. Very gently. Look by my front wheel.
Pip peeked under the bumper. And her eyes went wide.
Oh! Oh my! Everybody, please, please be quiet!
Quiet? Why quiet? Pip, what's down there?
Slowly, from under Bolt, a mother duck stepped out.
And behind her came one, two, three fluffy ducklings!
Ducks? You stopped the whole street for DUCKS?
They were walking to the pond. Then the honking started.
Scared ducks hide under the nearest thing. And that was me.
That was the quack! It was never Bertha's brakes!
So that's why you whispered. Hmph. Clever.
Loud noises make little ones freeze. So I stayed very still.
Oh, Bolt. You were helping. And we honked at you.
I called you bossy. Sorry, Bolt. That was not cool.
Thank you, Turbo. Now, everybody. Not one honk.
Nobody honked. Nobody zoomed. The whole street held its breath.
Mother duck waddled. The ducklings waddled after her. Waddle, waddle, waddle.
Go, little ducks! You can do it!
Shh, Pip! Whisper! We are a quiet street now!
Look at the last one. Tiny legs. Big effort. Respect.
And one by one, they splashed into the pond.
They made it! All four of them, safe in the pond!
Now hurry, everyone! The bell!
Bertha rolled to the school gate. Ding, ding, ding!
We made it! And the kids want to say thank you, Bolt!
I don't need a thank you. But next time, please listen first.
Listen first. Honk later. I can do that.
Before you blame someone, look at what they see!
Everybody laughed. Even Grumpy. Almost.
Then Bertha's driver hung a note on the school gate.
A crossing guard? Tomorrow? I'm getting that job, not Bolt!
Oh, Turbo. That job is all about going slow.
